title: Characters and induced-character classification of extremal positive harmonic functions on the discrete Heisenberg group for finitely supported group-generating positive measures
source_title: Positive harmonic functions on the Heisenberg group II
author: Yves Benoist
difficulty_reason: The cited Choquet--Deny theorem only classifies the abelian quotient or subgroup once central invariance or induction has been established. For general group-generating finite support, the author must prove that each extremal Heisenberg harmonic function falls into one of those two classes, including the case where the projected cone contains no line. The new weighted switching, negligible-trajectory and partition-generating-function estimates supply that nonroutine dichotomy before the final abelian reduction.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem1.1 on H3(Z), finite positive measure whose support generates the group, not necessarily a probability or semigroup-generating measure. Nonnegative nonzero extremal functions may vanish; classification includes translated finite induced characters of abelian subgroups. Complete new induction, central semi-invariance and central-invariance arguments read. Classical Choquet–Deny and Dynkin–Maljutov results are explicit existing foundations. No claim for arbitrary nilpotent groups or separate induced-character existence parameter variants. Display4.8 prints inversion exponent at least1, but the complete4.11 partition proof and generating series explicitly include exponent0; this is a bounded endpoint-index typo, with unchanged author source.
